Today does NOT resemble the 2023-24 trough on this instrument -- but ACP states the 2026 draft cuts will NOT affect transit counts, so absence of signal here is not evidence of an absent restriction.

Nine issues (May-2024..Dec-2024) carry 'the daily capacity has been adjusted to N vessels': 32 (May/Jun-24) -> 35 (Jul-24) -> 36 (Aug-24..Dec-24, unchanged over 5 issues), against a stated normal of 36-38/day. Declared capacity, slot ceilings and realised transits are THREE different quantities; do not reconcile to one figure.

MEASURED REFUTATION of the 'uploads/YYYY/MM tracks publication month (data+1)' heuristic. Holds 17 of 33 observed URLs (52%). Holds 16/19 from Jul-2024 on and 6/7 in 2026, but fails 15 of 21 in Nov-2023..Sep-2025 -- i.e. it fails hardest in the drought-trough window it was offered to speed up. 15 of the 16 misses collapse to a /uploads/YYYY/01/ catch-all bucket (Sep-2025 sits at /uploads/2025/01/); the 16th is Apr-2026 -> /uploads/2026/04/, the DATA month, and that URL was inside the 6-URL sample the rule was inferred from. Complete rule = one of three buckets => path is NOT constructible. Use the index (LOG row acp_complete_advisory_index_VALIDATED); it carries exact URLs and needs no rule.

METHOD. The claim 'no Gatun elevation in the monthly summaries' rests on literal PLD=0 and elevation=0. I REPRODUCE BOTH: zero occurrences of either token across all 33 issues. And a Gatun elevation is present anyway -- A-27-2024 writes 'Gatun Lake today is at 85.02 feet (25.91 m)', a sentence containing neither token. The keyword check was sound but was not an instrument for the claim it was used to settle: ACP does not write 'elevation', it writes 'is at N feet'. Same shape for draft -- the 8-issue sample behind the claim itself contained two numeric drafts (A-21-2024 47 ft, A-26-2026 47.5/48 ft). Corpus: draft in 6 issues, tonnage in 5, Gatun elevation in 1, ALL in the discretionary appended news article, NONE in the fixed-schema statistics table. Table-level absence is real and does not generalise to the document.
